name: Nomination Whist
description: Nomination Whist (commonly known as Oh Hell!) is an exact-bidding trick-taking game where players must predict exactly how many tricks they will win. The game features a unique dealing pattern that goes 'up and down the river'â€”starting with 1 card each, increasing to the maximum, then decreasing back to 1. The scoring rewards exact bids with a 10-point bonus plus tricks taken.

history.origins: Nomination Whist is known worldwide under many names including Oh Hell!, Oh Pshaw, Blackout, Up and Down the River, The Ten, and Grip. The game emerged in the early 20th century and spread internationally. The exact origin is unclear, but it became popular in Britain, America, and elsewhere.
timeline: Early 20th Century: Game emerges, possibly in Britain or America
Mid-20th Century: Spreads internationally with various local names
Present: One of the most popular exact-bidding games worldwide
history.cultural: Popular internationally as a social card game. The multiple names reflect its widespread adoptionâ€”'Oh Hell!' in America, 'Nomination Whist' in Britain, and various other names elsewhere.
history.evolution: The game evolved from standard Whist by adding the exact-bidding mechanic and the unique 'up and down' dealing pattern. Regional variants exist with different numbers of deals and special rules.

setup.dealing: 'Up and down the river': Deal 1 card each (round 1), then 2, 3, etc. up to maximum (typically 7-10 depending on players), then back down to 1. Total rounds = 2 Ã— max - 1.

rules.objective: Score the most points by making exactly the number of tricks bid.
rules.gameplay: Player left of dealer leads. Must follow suit if possible; may trump or discard if void. Highest trump wins trick; otherwise highest of led suit wins. Winner leads to next trick.
keyRules: Dealer's bid restrictedâ€”total cannot equal tricks available
Trump suit determined by turning card after deal

strategy.basic: Bid based on your hand strength and trump holding. With a weak hand, bid low (0 or 1). With strong trumps, bid more aggressively.
strategy.intermediate: The dealer restriction is keyâ€”if you're dealer, you may be forced into a difficult bid. Watch other bids and calculate what you're allowed to bid. Zero bids can be very effective with weak hands.
strategy.advanced: Card counting to track what's been played. Calculate probabilities of opponents' holdings based on their bids and play. In later rounds with fewer cards, exact calculation becomes possible.
tips: The dealer is at a disadvantage due to bid restrictionâ€”plan accordingly
Zero bids are powerful when you have no high cards or trumps
Remember: making your exact bid is worth 10 pointsâ€”often better to bid low and make it than bid high and miss
Track which cards have been played, especially in smaller hands
